cards.a: A software layer that creates and runs VMs by abstracting the underlying hardware. It schedules and isolates workloads running on it.

cards.q: What are the two hypervisor types and their examples?
cards.a: Type 1 (bare-metal) runs directly on hardware, e.g. ESXi, Hyper-V, KVM. Type 2 (hosted) runs on top of a host OS, e.g. VirtualBox, VMware Workstation.

cards.q: Which hypervisor type is the datacenter/cloud standard and why?
cards.a: Type 1 (bare-metal, e.g. ESXi and KVM), because it has near-native performance, minimal overhead, a smaller security surface, and direct hardware access.

cards.q: When is a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor appropriate?
cards.a: For desktop use, testing, and labs, where simple installation and dependence on a host OS are acceptable despite lower performance.
It schedules vCPUs, allocates memory, emulates or passes through I/O, isolates VMs from one another, and handles VM lifecycle management.

cards.q: What are the three virtualization models?
cards.a: Full virtualization (emulates hardware), paravirtualization (guest-aware), and hardware-assisted virtualization (uses CPU features like Intel VT-x). Modern hypervisors use hardware-assisted.
vCenter manages ESXi clusters, libvirt manages KVM, SCVMM manages Hyper-V, and cloud platforms orchestrate them via APIs.

cards.q: What command lists running VMs on an ESXi host?
cards.a: esxcli vm process list. Network views use esxcli network vswitch standard list.

cards.q: A VM won't start or I/O is slow on a hypervisor. What do you check?
cards.a: For a VM that won't start, check resource capacity; for slow I/O, check storage and the datastore. No vNIC points to the virtual switch and its network.

cards.q: Which hypervisor type is bare-metal and which is hosted?
cards.a: Type 1 is bare-metal (ESXi, Hyper-V, KVM); Type 2 is hosted on an OS (VirtualBox, VMware Workstation).

cards.q: Which virtualization model is the norm on modern hypervisors?
cards.a: Hardware-assisted virtualization (e.g., CPU VT-x), not full emulation or paravirtualization.

cards.q: How are vNICs connected to a hypervisor's network?
cards.a: Virtual switches (vSwitches) connect vNICs on the hypervisor; they are managed with platform-specific CLIs like esxcli network vswitch standard list.

cards.q: Match the quick review: Type 1, Type 2, ESXi, VirtualBox, job, model, management, use.
cards.a: Type 1 = bare-metal; Type 2 = hosted; ESXi = Type 1; VirtualBox = Type 2; job = schedule + isolate; model = hardware-assisted; management = vCenter; use = cloud/datacenter.
